definitionEn: to persuade or influence someone to do something
senseNote: Здесь — «убедить, побудить к действию» (обычно через стимул или уговоры). Медицинское «вызывать» (induce labour) — другое употребление.
situation: Explaining that someone was persuaded, often by a reward or clever argument, to do something they might not otherwise have done.

examples.text: Generous discounts [[induced]] thousands of shoppers to sign up before the deadline.
The company offered a generous bonus to [[induce]] senior staff not to join the strike.
Fear of failing the exam [[induced]] many students to start revising weeks earlier than usual.

texts: A small deposit is often enough to [[induce]] customers to commit to a purchase.
The manager used flattery to [[induce]] junior staff to work through the weekend.
Lawyers argued that the email was designed to [[induce]] readers to click a fraudulent link.

collocations: [[induced]] by the offer of a bonus

badCollocation.noteRu: После induce ставится инфинитив с to: induce someone to sign. Induce into (+ -ing) не говорят — это калька с «склонить к».

collocationTask.prompt: The company offered shares to ___ managers to stay.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Induce — «побудить» через стимул, как в этом предложении с акциями. Instruct — «дать указание», expect — «ожидать», warn — «предупредить»: не про склонение обещанием.

nuance.text: A tax rebate [[induced]] many households to install solar panels last year.
nuance.explanationRu: Induce — побудить выбором, обычно через стимул или выгоду. Force — заставить, лишив выбора; здесь люди сами решили ради выгоды, поэтому force не подходит.

reverse.text: The dictator [[forced]] farmers to hand over their entire harvest.
reverse.explanationRu: Если человека принуждают без всякого стимула и выбора — force. Induce предполагает, что решение всё же добровольное, пусть и под влиянием стимула.

fixIt.text: A free trial period [[provoked]] thousands of users to upgrade to the paid version.
fixIt.explanationRu: Provoke — вызвать реакцию, обычно негативную (спор, гнев). Здесь бесплатный период именно побудил людей выбрать платную версию — нужен induce.

wordFormation.text: The company's [[induction]] programme for new staff lasts a full week.

reply.context: A colleague messages: "Why did so many people suddenly switch to the new software?"
options: Mostly the free storage upgrade. It induced almost everyone to switch within a week.
It induced a huge storm that crashed half our servers.
The free storage upgrade did induce people into switching, innit, dunno why though.
reply.explanationRu: Induce someone to do something — «побудить сделать что-то» (через стимул). Во втором ответе induce ошибочно значит «вызвать событие», а третий слишком развязный для рабочего чата.

rewrite.original: A big discount persuaded her to buy the more expensive model.
rewrite.frame: A big discount ____ her to buy the more expensive model.
rewrite.explanationRu: Induce someone to do something — официальный синоним persuade.

definitionEn: to let someone have or do what they want, especially as a favour
senseNote: Здесь — «потакать, идти навстречу» (indulge someone / indulge me for a moment). Более частое indulge in something («побаловать себя») — другое значение.
situation: Agreeing to let someone do or have something they want, often as a kind favour or because you find it hard to refuse.

examples.text: Just this once, [[indulge]] me and let's take the scenic route instead of the motorway.
Grandparents often [[indulge]] their grandchildren with treats that parents would normally forbid.
The waiter offered to [[indulge]] our request for a table by the window, even though we hadn't booked.

texts: Please [[indulge]] me for a moment while I explain the whole plan.
The hotel is happy to [[indulge]] unusual requests from long-standing guests.
A good manager will sometimes [[indulge]] a colleague's need to vent before offering advice.

badCollocation.noteRu: Indulge — переходный глагол без предлога перед человеком или просьбой: indulge your friend's request. To здесь лишнее.

collocationTask.prompt: The teacher decided to ___ the children's request for extra playtime.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Indulge — «потакать, идти навстречу желанию». Induce — «побудить сделать что-то», introduce — «представить, ввести», instruct — «дать указание»: не подходят по смыслу.

nuance.text: Her uncle always [[indulged]] her love of dramatic stories, however unlikely they sounded.
nuance.explanationRu: Indulge — охотно потакать, поддерживать чьё-то желание. Tolerate — просто мириться с чем-то, не обязательно одобряя. Дядя здесь именно потакает, а не просто терпит.

reverse.text: He merely [[tolerated]] his neighbour's loud parties, without ever actually enjoying them.
reverse.explanationRu: Tolerate — мириться, не обязательно с удовольствием. Indulge подразумевает более тёплое, снисходительное отношение, а сосед его явно не одобряет.

fixIt.text: To keep the peace, he usually [[obeyed]] his sister's constant requests for favours.
fixIt.explanationRu: Obey — подчиняться, выполнять приказ. Родственник, который просто уступает капризам, indulges их, не «подчиняется» им.

wordFormation.text: [[Indulgent]] parents sometimes find it hard to say no, even when they know they should.

reply.context: Your roommate says: "I know it's late, but could we watch just one more episode?"
options: Sure, let's indulge you tonight. One more, then bed.
Sure, I'll indulge the TV so it doesn't overheat.
Your request for extended viewing shall be indulged, madam.
reply.explanationRu: Indulge someone — «уступить, потакать» чьей-то просьбе. Indulge the TV — бессмыслица, а третий ответ звучит как объявление дворецкого, а не разговор соседей.

rewrite.original: The waiter kindly agreed to our unusual request for a corner table.
rewrite.frame: The waiter kindly ____ our unusual request for a corner table.

definitionEn: an unfair difference between groups of people in wealth, opportunity or treatment
situation: Discussing unfair gaps between rich and poor, or between different groups, in income, education or opportunities.

examples.text: Growing [[inequality]] between rich and poor neighbourhoods worries many city planners.
The report highlights [[inequality]] in access to healthcare across different regions.
Campaigners marched to protest against gender [[inequality]] in the tech industry.

texts: Economists warn that rising [[inequality]] could slow long-term growth.
The novel explores class [[inequality]] in a small English village.
Reducing [[inequality]] between regions remains a key government promise.

badCollocation.noteRu: Inequality — про группы, доходы, возможности в масштабе общества. Разница между двумя конкретными людьми — просто a difference, не inequality.

collocationTask.prompt: The report focuses on income ___ between men and women.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Устойчивое сочетание — income inequality. Unfairness, dissimilarity и irregularity с income так не говорят.

nuance.text: Critics say the pay gap reflects deep-seated [[inequality]], not simply diversity of roles.
nuance.explanationRu: Inequality — несправедливое неравенство (в доходах, правах). Diversity — просто разнообразие, различие, не обязательно несправедливое. Разрыв в зарплате — именно inequality, а не diversity ролей.

reverse.text: The company is proud of the cultural [[diversity]] within its design team.
reverse.explanationRu: Просто разнообразие культур внутри команды — diversity, это не про несправедливость. Inequality говорит именно о неравенстве, а не о разнообразии.

fixIt.text: The UN report warns that global [[difference]] in vaccine access could cost millions of lives.
fixIt.explanationRu: Difference — нейтральное «различие». Несправедливый разрыв в доступе к вакцинам — inequality.

reply.context: A classmate says: "Why does our economics class spend so much time on the wealth gap?"
options: Because inequality shapes almost everything else in the economy, from health to education.
Because inequality means everyone earns exactly the same amount.
One must acknowledge that inequality remains a subject of considerable academic import.
reply.explanationRu: Inequality — «неравенство», а не «равенство» (это было бы противоположным смыслом), как ошибочно во втором ответе. Третий звучит как отрывок из научной статьи, а не реплика однокурснику.

rewrite.original: Poor children in this country have far fewer opportunities than rich ones.
rewrite.frame: There is significant ____ of opportunity between poor and rich children in this country.

definitionEn: widely known because of something bad, shocking or criminal
situation: Describing a person, place or event that is very well known, but for doing something wrong, criminal or shocking.

examples.text: The hotel became [[infamous]] after three separate scandals in a single year.
He remains [[infamous]] for insulting three world leaders at the same dinner.
The prison is [[infamous]] for its harsh conditions and frequent escapes.

texts: The area was once [[infamous]] for street crime, though it has changed a lot.
She became [[infamous]] overnight after the leaked recording went viral.
The castle is [[infamous]] for the ghost stories attached to it.

badCollocation.noteRu: Infamous значит «печально известный», а не просто «известный». Хороший ресторан с хорошей репутацией — famous или well-known, не infamous.

collocationTask.prompt: The gang leader became ___ for his cruelty.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Infamous — «печально известный» специально о плохом. Renowned, respected и admired — с положительным оттенком, с cruelty («жестокость») не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The building is [[infamous]] for the tragic fire that killed twelve workers in 1911.
nuance.explanationRu: Infamous — известен именно из-за чего-то плохого. Famous нейтрально или положительно, и «знаменитое из-за трагического пожара» с ним звучит нелепо-жизнерадостно.

reverse.text: The chef is [[famous]] for his delicate seafood dishes.
reverse.explanationRu: Известность за хорошее — famous. Infamous предполагает дурную славу, а изысканные блюда — явно не она.

fixIt.text: The building is now [[popular]] for the fire that killed several workers a century ago.
fixIt.explanationRu: Popular — про то, что нравится людям. Печальная известность из-за трагедии — infamous.

wordFormation.text: The town's [[infamy]] as a smugglers' haven drew curious visitors for generations.

reply.context: A tourist asks: "I heard this old prison has a strange reputation. What happened here?"
options: It's infamous, actually — dozens of prisoners tried to escape through that very tunnel.
It's infamous for its beautiful gardens and friendly staff.
The premises are widely regarded as infamous, as documented in the official gazette.
reply.explanationRu: Infamous — известность из-за плохого, как побеги из тюрьмы. Красивые сады не делают место infamous, а третий ответ звучит как официальный документ, а не ответ туристу.

rewrite.original: Everyone in the country knows the senator's name because of the corruption scandal.
rewrite.frame: The senator is ____ throughout the country because of the corruption scandal.

definitionEn: a baby or very young child, especially in official, medical or legal language
senseNote: Формальное/официальное слово для «младенца»: infant mortality, infant welfare. В обычном разговоре о своём ребёнке чаще говорят baby.
situation: Talking about babies or very young children in official statistics, medical reports or laws, rather than in everyday family conversation.

examples.text: The clinic offers free vaccinations for [[infants]] under one year old.
Studies show that reading aloud to [[infants]] helps their language development later on.
The report tracks [[infant]] mortality rates across different regions of the country.

texts: The charity funds nutrition programmes for [[infant]] health in rural areas.
Doctors recommend delaying solid food until an [[infant]] is around six months old.
The museum has a small exhibit on [[infant]] care in Victorian times.

badCollocation.noteRu: О своём ребёнке в быту говорят my baby, а не my infant — infant звучит слишком официально или по-медицински для разговора о своей семье.

collocationTask.prompt: The country has one of the lowest ___ mortality rates in the world.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Устойчивый термин статистики — infant mortality rate. Young, junior и minor с mortality rate не сочетаются.

nuance.text: The report focuses on [[infant]] nutrition programmes funded by the ministry of health.
nuance.explanationRu: Infant — официальное, статистическое слово. Baby — обычное, бытовое: baby nutrition в официальном докладе звучит слишком неформально.

reverse.text: She spent the whole afternoon playing with her sister's new [[baby]].
reverse.explanationRu: В быту, о своём или чужом ребёнке, говорят baby. Infant в этой фразе звучало бы неестественно официально.

fixIt.text: The government report on [[baby]] mortality rates was published this week.
fixIt.explanationRu: В официальных отчётах и статистике используется infant, а не бытовое baby: infant mortality rate.

wordFormation.text: The recycling programme is still in its [[infancy]], but early results look promising.

reply.context: A friend asks: "Why does this article keep saying 'infant' instead of just 'baby'?"
options: It's a medical article, and infant is the more formal, technical word for baby.
Infant means a much older child, like a teenager.
Infant refers strictly to baby animals, never humans.
reply.explanationRu: Infant — формальный синоним baby, обычно в официальных и медицинских текстах. Оно не значит «подросток» и относится именно к людям.

definitionEn: to spread a feeling, mood or attitude to the people around you, often quickly
senseNote: Здесь — переносное «заражать» настроением или чувством. Буквальное «заражать вирусом, бактерией» — более базовое значение.
situation: Describing how one person's mood, enthusiasm or laughter quickly spreads to everyone around them.

examples.text: Her excitement about the trip soon [[infected]] the rest of the office.
The captain's calm confidence [[infected]] the whole team before the final.
Panic quickly [[infected]] the crowd when the fire alarm went off.

texts: A single cynical remark can [[infect]] an entire meeting with negativity.
Good humour can [[infect]] even the most stressful workplace.
One person's fear can [[infect]] a whole crowd within minutes.

badCollocation.text: the excitement [[infected]] into the whole stadium
badCollocation.noteRu: После infect не нужен предлог into: the excitement infected the whole stadium (без into). Есть другое слово, spread, которое действительно берёт into/through.

collocationTask.prompt: Her enthusiasm for the project quickly ___ the rest of the team.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Infect — «заражать» (в том числе настроением). Inject нужен предлог with (inject enthusiasm INTO), infest — про вредителей и паразитов, inflict — «причинять» (обычно боль) с предлогом on.

nuance.text: His nervousness before the interview [[infected]] the whole waiting room.
nuance.explanationRu: Infect (переносное) — заразить чувством так, что оно распространяется на всех вокруг. Affect — просто повлиять, необязательно передать то же чувство другим.

reverse.text: The delay [[affected]] everyone's plans for the evening.
reverse.explanationRu: Просто повлиять на что-то — affect. Infect в переносном смысле — именно «заразить» своим настроением, а не просто повлиять.

fixIt.text: Her nervous energy [[affected]] the entire cast right before opening night, and soon everyone was pacing backstage.
fixIt.explanationRu: Affect — нейтрально «повлиять». Если нервозность буквально передалась всем, как зараза, — infected.

wordFormation.text: Her [[infectious]] enthusiasm made even the shyest students want to join in.

reply.context: A colleague says: "Why is everyone in the office suddenly so obsessed with this new game?"
options: Sam started playing it, and honestly, his enthusiasm just infected the whole team.
The game infected everyone's laptops with a virus over the weekend.
Enthusiasm for said game has evidently infected the workforce, as per observation.
reply.explanationRu: Infect — переносно «заразить» настроением, как в первом ответе. Во втором это буквальный компьютерный вирус, а третий звучит как канцелярский отчёт, а не разговор с коллегой.

rewrite.original: Her laughter spread through the room until everyone was giggling.
rewrite.frame: Her laughter ____ the whole room until everyone was giggling.
rewrite.explanationRu: Infect (переносное) — «заразить» смехом или настроением всех вокруг.

definitionEn: to make someone suffer something unpleasant, such as pain, damage or punishment
situation: Talking about someone or something causing pain, damage or punishment to a person, usually deliberately or as a result of carelessness.

examples.text: The storm [[inflicted]] serious damage on dozens of coastal towns overnight.
The judge can [[inflict]] a heavier sentence if the crime involved a weapon.
Years of neglect had [[inflicted]] lasting damage on the historic building.

texts: A single mistake here could [[inflict]] lasting damage on the company's reputation.
The court has the power to [[inflict]] fines of up to ten thousand pounds.
Poor planning can [[inflict]] real hardship on ordinary families.

badCollocation.noteRu: Inflict — только про что-то плохое или неприятное: боль, ущерб, наказание. Об одолжении так не говорят; правильно — do someone a favour.

collocationTask.prompt: The defeat ___ serious damage on the team's confidence.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Inflict damage on — «причинить ущерб». Afflict обычно значит «поражать» (болезнью, бедой) и не сочетается с on в этом смысле, inflate — «раздувать», conflicted — «испытывающий противоречивые чувства».

nuance.text: The dictator's army [[inflicted]] terrible suffering on the civilian population.
nuance.explanationRu: Inflict — причинять страдание кому-то другому (inflict something ON someone). Suffer — самому испытывать страдание; здесь именно армия причиняет, а не переносит.

reverse.text: Thousands of civilians [[suffered]] terrible hardship during the siege.
reverse.explanationRu: Suffer — переносить страдания на себе. Inflict — причинять их кому-то другому; здесь именно мирные жители страдают, а не причиняют страдания.

fixIt.text: The referee's harsh decision [[suffered]] real damage on the team's morale.
fixIt.explanationRu: Suffer — испытывать страдание самому. Причинить ущерб кому-то другому — inflict damage on someone.

reply.context: A friend says: "The final scene of that film was so brutal, I could barely watch."
options: I know — the director really doesn't hold back when it comes to inflicting pain on the characters.
I know — the characters really inflicted a lovely afternoon on each other.
Indeed, considerable suffering was inflicted upon the viewership, as critics duly noted.
reply.explanationRu: Inflict — причинять что-то плохое, как боль в первом ответе. «Причинить приятный день» бессмысленно, а третий ответ звучит как театральная рецензия, а не разговор с другом.

rewrite.original: The scandal caused serious harm to the company's reputation.
rewrite.frame: The scandal ____ serious harm on the company's reputation.

definitionEn: having a lot of power to affect how people think, behave or make decisions
situation: Describing a person, idea or organisation with the power to change how other people think, behave or make important decisions.

examples.text: She is one of the most [[influential]] scientists working on climate change today.
The magazine remains hugely [[influential]] among young fashion designers.
His early mentor proved [[influential]] in shaping his entire career.

texts: Social media has become [[influential]] in shaping political opinion.
Her grandmother was a quietly [[influential]] figure in the local community.
The report proved [[influential]], leading to changes in national policy.

collocations: one of the most [[influential]] people in

badCollocation.noteRu: Influential — про людей, идеи и организации с реальным влиянием. Сильную простуду по-английски называют a bad/heavy cold, не influential.

collocationTask.prompt: She is widely regarded as one of the most ___ economists of her generation.
collocationTask.explanationRu: После most нужно прилагательное — influential. Influenced и influencing — формы глагола, influence — существительное; они не подходят после most economists.

nuance.text: The professor is far more [[influential]] in the field than many better-known writers.
nuance.explanationRu: Influential — реально меняющий взгляды и решения других. Famous — просто известный, необязательно оказывающий влияние на идеи. Здесь именно противопоставляются известность и реальное влияние.

reverse.text: The actor is [[famous]] worldwide, even though critics rarely take his films seriously.
reverse.explanationRu: Famous — просто известный многим. Influential предполагает реальное влияние на мысли или решения, а не просто узнаваемость.

fixIt.text: Although she avoided the spotlight, her ideas were quietly [[famous]] in shaping how a generation of teachers taught reading.
fixIt.explanationRu: Famous — просто известный. «Влиять на что-то, формировать» — это influential, а не famous.

wordFormation.text: Few people outside the industry have ever heard of her, yet she remains hugely [[influential]] behind the scenes.

reply.context: A student asks: "Why do we have to study this philosopher? Nobody's heard of him."
options: True, he's not famous, but he was hugely influential — modern ethics wouldn't exist without his ideas.
Good point, he wasn't influential at all, so let's skip the whole chapter.
His influential status has been duly certified by three separate academic committees.
reply.explanationRu: Influential — реально повлиявший на дальнейшие идеи, даже если не «раскручен». Второй ответ противоречит смыслу вопроса, а третий звучит как бюрократическая справка, а не ответ студенту.

rewrite.original: This book changed the way an entire generation of writers thought about fiction.
rewrite.frame: This book was extremely ____ in shaping how an entire generation of writers thought about fiction.
rewrite.explanationRu: Influential in shaping — «оказавший влияние на формирование».
